problem.issuerFirst.message: Enter the issuer URL first, like {pattern}.
problem.issuerFirst.note: pattern: the preset's issuer pattern, a URL

problem.beforeTest.note: blockers: the sentences of what's missing (blocker.*), one after another

problem.enableBeforeEnforcing: Enable {name} before enforcing it for a domain.
problem.confirmEnforcement: Confirm who keeps password access before turning enforcement on.
problem.enforcedElsewhere: {name} already enforces one of these domains. Turn it off there first.
problem.disableBeforeSwitch: Disable {name} before switching it to another preset, or add a new provider.
problem.name: Give the provider a name people recognise on the sign-in page.
problem.issuerURL: Enter the issuer as an https URL, like {pattern}.
problem.scopes: Scopes are single words like openid, profile or groups.
problem.jitWorkspace: Pick the workspace new people join.
problem.role: Pick a role of that workspace.
problem.jitOwner: New accounts can't become Owner automatically.
problem.group: Enter the IdP group (an object ID for Entra ID).
problem.groupMapped: Group {group} is already mapped in that workspace.
problem.mappingOwner: Owner can't be granted by a group mapping. Transfer ownership in the workspace's settings instead.
problem.notMember: You aren't a member of {workspace}, so you can't grant its roles. Ask an Owner of that workspace to add the mapping.

problem.cantGrant.message: You can't grant {role} in {workspace}: you don't hold {permission} there. Ask an Owner of that workspace to add the mapping.
problem.cantGrant.note: permission: a permission key like campaigns:send, never translated

problem.githubOrg: GitHub organization names use letters, digits and single hyphens, like acme-eng.
problem.tenant: Use common, organizations, consumers or a tenant ID.
problem.socialSecret: {provider} needs a client ID and secret before it can be turned on.

blocker.discovery.message: Run a successful discovery test of the issuer URL.
blocker.discovery.note: what's missing before a provider can be enabled or tested

grant.notMember.message: you aren't a member of {workspace}, so you can't grant its roles
grant.notMember.note: why a role can't be picked in a mapping: the option's tooltip and the field's error; lower-case and without a period in English

grant.missing: you can't grant {role} in {workspace}: you don't hold {permission} there
grant.ownerSSO: Owner can't be granted by SSO; transfer ownership in workspace settings.

twoFactor.amr.message: Counted when the ID token's amr claim includes mfa; otherwise the person's own second factor is asked for
twoFactor.amr.note: how a provider satisfies two-factor; amr and mfa are claim values, never translated

keeps.passwordTwoFactor.note: how a break-glass Owner still signs in while SSO is enforced

keeps.nothing: nothing but SSO (no password or passkey)

sample.notSentBy.note: a claim the identity provider didn't send; idp: its short name (Entra ID, Okta, the IdP)

sample.verifiedForDomains: treated as verified for allowed domains
sample.unverified: treated as unverified: add an allowed domain to trust it
sample.overage: too many groups: {name} sent an overage link instead

outcome.rejected.note: the test sign-in's “What this sign-in would do”: a row's label

detail.newAccount: No account for {email} yet · a just-in-time account is created at the first sign-in
detail.removed: {workspace}: leaves the workspace · no longer in group “{group}”, which granted {role}
detail.staysOwner: {workspace}: stays Owner · mappings never change an Owner
detail.deactivated: {workspace}: membership is deactivated · the mapping doesn't reactivate it
detail.stays: {workspace}: stays {role} {source, select, group {from group “{group}”} other {(JIT default)}}
detail.joins: {workspace}: joins as {role} {source, select, group {from group “{group}”} other {(JIT default)}}
detail.demoted: {workspace}: {change} {source, select, group {from group “{group}”} other {(JIT default)}}. The direct assignment is replaced at their next sign-in; review the mapping if that's not intended.
detail.mappingsInactive: No groups claim · {count, plural, one {the group mapping doesn't apply} other {the # group mappings don't apply}}

mfa.amr.message: amr includes mfa · counts as two-factor via IdP
mfa.amr.note: starts with the claim's name, amr, shown in code type

mfa.amrWithout: amr is {amr} · no second factor, so the person's own is asked for
mfa.noAmr: No amr claim · the person's own second factor is asked for

enforce.password.note: how someone signs in today, in the enforcement dialog: “Acme SSO · Password · passkey”

audit.saved.note: the audit log's summary of a saved SSO provider: facts joined with ·

audit.mappings: {count, plural, one {# group mapping} other {# group mappings}}
audit.keys: {count, plural, one {# signing key} other {# signing keys}}

reason.jit.note: the audit log's reason of an entry SSO wrote; name: the provider's name

reason.leftGroupDefault: no longer in {name} group “{group}” · just-in-time default role of {name} SSO
reason.leftGroup: no longer in {name} group “{group}”, which granted {role}

flow.expired.message: This sign-in link expired or was already used. Start again.
flow.expired.note: why a sign-in with an identity provider failed: the audit log and the test sign-in

flow.otherBrowser: This sign-in was started in another browser. Start again here.
flow.broke: Something broke on our side while finishing the sign-in.

flow.singleSignOn.note: names the sign-in on the sign-in page's error when its provider is unknown: “Single sign-on couldn't sign you in”

flow.notConfigured: {name} has no client ID or secret yet.
flow.secretUnreadable: The client secret can't be decrypted with this server's key. Replace it in Instance admin › SSO.

flow.discoveryFailed.note: error: what the library reported, in English

flow.ssoOff: Single sign-on is turned off on this instance.
flow.otherProvider: This callback belongs to another provider.

flow.idpError.note: error and description: the identity provider's own words

flow.turnedOff: {name} was turned off during the sign-in.
flow.signInToLink: Sign in again to link an identity.
flow.identityInUse: This {name} account is already linked to another ReputeCast account.
flow.alreadyLinked: Your account already has a {name} sign-in. Unlink it first to link another.
flow.noIDToken: The identity provider returned no ID token. Check that the openid scope is requested.
flow.nonce: The ID token's nonce doesn't match this sign-in. Start again.
flow.claims: The ID token's claims couldn't be read.
flow.noSubject: The ID token has no sub claim.
flow.noEmail: {name} sent no email claim ("{claim}"). Check the claim mapping.
flow.domain: email domain not allowed for {name} SSO
flow.noAccount: no account for {email} and automatic accounts (JIT) are off
flow.unconfirmed: {name} didn't confirm that {email} is verified, so no account is created.
flow.allowlist: email domain not on the allowlist for automatic accounts
social.notConfigured: {name} sign-in has no client ID or secret yet.
social.googleDiscovery: Google's discovery document couldn't be loaded: {error}
social.microsoftDiscovery: Microsoft's discovery document couldn't be loaded: {error}
social.off: {name} sign-in is turned off on this instance.
social.notLinked: no account is linked to this {name} sign-in
social.noAccount: no account for {email}; {name} sign-in never creates one
social.tenant: The Microsoft token's issuer doesn't match its tenant.
social.githubEmails: GitHub didn't return the email addresses (HTTP {status}). The user:email scope is needed.
social.githubNoEmail: Your GitHub account has no verified primary email.
social.githubOrgCheck: GitHub didn't answer the organization check: {error}
social.githubRestricted: The GitHub organization {org} restricts third-party apps. An owner of {org} must approve ReputeCast's OAuth app.
social.githubNotInOrg: GitHub sign-in is limited to members of the organization {org}.

discovery.url.message: Enter the issuer as a full URL, like {example}.
discovery.url.note: the discovery test of an issuer URL

discovery.https: The issuer must use https. Plain http is only accepted for localhost.

discovery.noAnswer.message: The issuer didn't answer: {why, select, timeout {no answer within 8 seconds.} dns {the host name doesn't resolve (DNS).} refused {the connection was refused.} tls {its TLS certificate isn't valid ({error}).} other {{error}.}}
discovery.noAnswer.note: error: what the network library reported, in English

discovery.status.note: follows the discovery document's URL on the setup page: “…/openid-configuration returned 404 Not Found”; statusText is HTTP's own, in English

discovery.json.message: returned something that isn't a discovery document (invalid JSON).
discovery.json.note: follows the discovery document's URL, like discovery.status

discovery.noIssuer: The discovery document has no issuer.
discovery.issuerMismatch: The document's issuer is {reported}, not {entered}. Use exactly the issuer it reports.
discovery.endpoints: The discovery document is missing the authorization, token or JWKS endpoint.
discovery.jwksNoAnswer: The JWKS endpoint didn't answer: {why, select, timeout {no answer within 8 seconds.} dns {the host name doesn't resolve (DNS).} refused {the connection was refused.} tls {its TLS certificate isn't valid ({error}).} other {{error}.}}
discovery.jwksKeys: The JWKS endpoint returned {status} without signing keys.

preset.google.app.note: where the redirect URI goes: “add this to the {app}”, “Paste the secret from the {app}”

preset.google.groupsHint: Google doesn't send a groups claim over OIDC. Map people by email domain (JIT default role) or assign roles individually in Team.
preset.google.trustedTwoFactor: Trusted from Google (2-Step Verification enforced in Workspace)
preset.entra.discoveryHint: Entra ID issuer URLs use the tenant ID (a GUID) or the verified domain, for example https://login.microsoftonline.com/7c1a2b3d-…/v2.0. Find it under Entra ID → Overview → Tenant ID.
preset.entra.groupsHint: Groups arrive as a token claim, not a scope: turn on the groups claim in the app registration's token configuration.

preset.entra.groupsMissingHint.message: In the Entra app registration open Token configuration → Add groups claim and include security groups in the ID token. If a user is in more than 200 groups, Entra sends an overage link instead; use app roles then.
preset.entra.groupsMissingHint.note: the menu path after “open” is shown in bold, up to “and”

preset.entra.trustedTwoFactor: Trusted from Entra ID (MFA enforced by Conditional Access)
preset.okta.discoveryHint: Okta issuer URLs are your Okta domain, or an authorization server such as https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default. Find it under Security → API → Authorization Servers.
preset.okta.groupsHint: Add a groups claim to the authorization server (filter: matches regex .*) and request the groups scope.
preset.okta.groupsMissingHint: In Okta open Security → API → your authorization server → Claims and add a groups claim to the ID token, then request the groups scope.
preset.okta.trustedTwoFactor: Trusted from Okta (MFA enforced by a sign-on policy)
preset.keycloak.discoveryHint: Keycloak issuer URLs end with the realm, for example https://sso.acme.io/realms/acme.
preset.keycloak.groupsHint: Add a Group Membership mapper to the client (token claim name groups, full group path off).
preset.keycloak.groupsMissingHint: In Keycloak open Clients → your client → Client scopes → dedicated scope and add a Group Membership mapper with the claim name groups.
preset.keycloak.trustedTwoFactor: Trusted from Keycloak (OTP required by the realm's browser flow)
preset.authentik.discoveryHint: Authentik issuer URLs end with the application slug and a slash, for example https://auth.acme.io/application/o/reputecast/.
preset.authentik.groupsHint: Authentik sends the user's groups in the groups claim of the profile scope.
preset.authentik.groupsMissingHint: In Authentik check that the provider's scope mappings include the default profile mapping, which sends groups.
preset.authentik.trustedTwoFactor: Trusted from Authentik (MFA stage in the authentication flow)

preset.oidc.name.note: the preset for any OpenID Connect identity provider

preset.oidc.shortName.note: used in sentences: “not sent by the IdP”, “Opens the IdP in a popup”

preset.oidc.discoveryHint: The issuer is the URL before /.well-known/openid-configuration.
preset.oidc.groupsHint: Configure your IdP to send the user's groups as a claim in the ID token.
preset.oidc.groupsMissingHint: Configure your IdP to add the user's groups to the ID token, then run the test again.
